notes: §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR2 requires of an external file connector that its file description entries "specify the same values for integer-1 or integer-2 and integer-3" and that, "If the RECORD clause is not specified, all record description entries associated with this file connector must be the same length". At COBOL-85 FileDescriptionIdentity asks both halves (kb/Work PB5387), as the other 1985 file description clauses are asked (PB5300): the RECORD row compares the operands of the clauses the entries write (Format 1's integer-1; Formats 2 and 3's pair, an omitted or refused operand agreeing with anything; the format is part of the value), and the RECORD-LENGTH row requires of the entries that write none that every record description is one length (an entry whose own descriptions differ is refused against itself) and that the entries agree in it; each disagreement is COBOL6847 at the entry. A clause against no clause is not compared: the text states each half among the entries it describes. Witnesses: the three refusals and the agreeing Format 2 against Format 3 pair. The rule is the same mechanism as the BLOCK CONTAINS and LABEL RECORDS arms; later editions state their own rule (§2023:13.4.5.4 GR2 d), not asked here.

next.reason: 1985: for an external file connector every FD must 'specify the same values for integer-1 or integer-2 and integer-3', and 'If the RECORD clause is not specified, all record description entries associated with this file connector must be the same length.' 2023 states only §2023:13.4.5.4 GR2 d) 'All file description entries shall have the same smallest and largest record size'; without a RECORD clause each FD's sizes come from its implicit clause (§2023:13.18.43.4 GR5), and no 2023 rule requires the record descriptions to be one length. An external file whose FDs omit the RECORD clause and describe records of different lengths with the same smallest and largest sizes is now conforming: looser.
